brief.topic: The PoC was cheap. Production costs far more. Why?
brief.audience: PMs and leads taking a GenAI PoC to production

coreInsight: PoC costs hide four multipliers — real volume, longer context, retries and tool calls, and eval runs — so model cost per completed task at full scale before you commit.

hooks.text: Your PoC bill isn’t your real bill.
hooks.notes: Plain, credible and specific to the moment teams get surprised.

hooks.text: The PoC was cheap. That’s the problem.
hooks.notes: Intriguing but the “why” takes a beat to arrive.

hooks.text: Four numbers your AI cost estimate is missing.

caption.opening: A PoC runs a few people, short prompts and one call per question. Production runs none of those.
body:
What multiplies between the demo and the launch:
→ volume: every user, every day
→ context: retrieved documents and chat history make prompts longer
→ retries and tool calls: one task can mean several model calls
→ eval runs: you re-test on every prompt or model change
Model this before the business case goes in. The unit that matters to finance is cost per completed task, not cost per call.

claims.text: Production GenAI costs are driven by volume, context length, calls per task (retries, tools) and evaluation runs, which PoC costs rarely reflect.
